coverage: Whole image once for layout; half a once line by line against both C and H, covering the date, salutation, every word/letter/accent/punctuation of all four paragraphs, all three list rows and their cancellation, separate VI B line, every Roman reference and lowered B, all overprints/deletions and closing. Half b once against both witnesses covers the overlapping last two body lines, closing, full blank lower field, both lower margins and archive 15. notes.text: The letter is dated Massy le 3.11.1970 and addressed Cher Verdier. It says the writer has scarcely attended to Math for three months and twice qualifies recollection with Si je me rappelle bien. The outstanding-parts list cancels IV, par.9 et suivants and retains V and VI par.5 et suivants.
notes.basis: Observation: date, salutation, paragraph 1, list, opening of paragraph 2. The cancelled list row was checked in crop 01; IV, comma, par.9 and et suivants are readable.

notes.text: The first recollection in paragraph 2 concerns a drafted exposé needing modifications discussed before Verdier’s departure. Its Roman reference is overtyped and is not assigned a unique final value in this reading.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 2 first three lines and crop 02; no inference from the publication sequence.

notes.text: The writer thinks Verdier has Saint Donat’s VI B and says he is sending the same author’s Appendix to XVII. He says he had apparemment read its first pages and asks for its return to himself or St Donat with annotations and comments.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 2, standalone VI B and continuation. These are the source’s stated beliefs and requests, not independently verified possession or reading.

notes.text: The writer presumes Verdier has an exemplar of the XVII impression. XVIII is described as typed directly on paper for offset; the typing is finished and Deligne is censé la corriger. The Stencils initial and the la/il superposition are left explicitly uncertain.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 3, half a and crops 05–06.

notes.text: The writer asks for progress on drafting and reading VI B, wants V, VI and VI with a lowered B available within deux, trois mois, and requests the addressee’s intention and expected completion time. The cancelled name is not identified by context.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 4. The third reference has a visibly lowered B; tous in en tous cas is source spelling. No mathematical claim or proof is checked.

notes.text: The apparently heavy il at the end of paragraph 2’s first physical line remains plain il: crop 03 does not establish a distinct underletter or reliably separated duplicate contour. Dark type alone is not treated as a correction. The o in Pourrais, by contrast, has two distinctly displaced closed contours.
notes.basis: Observation: crops 03 and 04; typographical inspection only.

notes.text: The entire lower blank field and both margins were inspected. There is no signature, added prose, diagram, or drawing. The lower-left handwritten 15 is treated as the archive sheet number. The left-side vertical mark near the last paragraph follows the paper damage, not a transcribed insertion pointer. H’s carbon-copy and overtyping descriptions are editorial notes, not source text.
notes.basis: Observation: whole image, halves a and b. No claim is made about the material carbon-copy generation.

notes.text: All visible punctuation and line-end word divisions were inspected. The lectu-/re line division is joined; Pourrais tu has no hyphen, Ecris-moi has no initial accent, VI B . retains its visible period, and en tous cas retains s. Ordinary spacing around punctuation and H’s wrapping are not counted as discrepancies.
notes.basis: Observation: both halves, with crop 04 for Pourrais tu. No mathematical checking occurred; check_events is intentionally empty.
